name: Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM)
short description: A scanning electron microscope (SEM) is a type of electron microscope that produces images of a sample by scanning the surface with a focused beam of electrons. The electrons interact with atoms in the sample, producing various signals that contain information about the surface topography and composition. The electron beam is scanned in a raster scan pattern, and the position of the beam is combined with the intensity of the detected signal to produce an image. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: NIH Image to ImageJ: 25 years of image analysis (Nature Methods, 2012), Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles 2018 (MISEV2018): a position statement of the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles and update of the MISEV2014 guidelines (Journal of Extracellular Vesicles, 2018), Lead Iodide Perovskite Sensitized All, Solid, State Submicron Thin Film Mesoscopic Solar Cell with Efficiency Exceeding 9% (Scientific Reports, 2012), Genome sequencing in microfabricated high, density picolitre reactors (Nature, 2005), Structural absorption by barbule microstructures of super black bird of paradise feathers (Nature Communications, 2017)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) for materials science research.

name: Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM)
short description: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is a microscopy technique in which a beam of electrons is transmitted through a specimen to form an image. The specimen is most often an ultrathin section less than 100 nm thick or a suspension on a grid. An image is formed from the interaction of the electrons with the sample as the beam is transmitted through the specimen. Equipment at University in The Pirbright Institute (UK).
typical applications: A pneumonia outbreak associated with a new coronavirus of probable bat origin (Nature, 2020), Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles 2018 (MISEV2018): a position statement of the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles and update of the MISEV2014 guidelines (Journal of Extracellular Vesicles, 2018), Double, slit photoelectron interference in strong, field ionization of the neon dimer (Nature Communications, 2018), Lead Iodide Perovskite Sensitized All, Solid, State Submicron Thin Film Mesoscopic Solar Cell with Efficiency Exceeding 9% (Scientific Reports, 2012), Culture of Human Endothelial Cells Derived from Umbilical Veins. IDENTIFICATION BY MORPHOLOGIC AND IMMUNOLOGIC CRITERIA (Journal of Clinical Investigation, 1973)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) for materials science research.

name: Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer (FTIR)
short description: FTIR spectroscopy is an analytical technique used for structural estimation and identification of organic and inorganic compounds by measuring infrared absorption. It is frequently used for qualification and quantification of constituents in solid, liquid, and gas samples across pharmaceutical, chemical, and materials science applications.
typical applications: Identification and structural analysis of organic compounds, Polymer and plastics characterization, Pharmaceutical quality control and raw material verification, Contaminant and foreign, particle analysis, Environmental monitoring and gas analysis
research-oriented use: 1. Identifying microplastic contaminants in marine water samples using ATR, FTIR and automated particle analysis. 2. Verifying the identity and purity of active pharmaceutical ingredients against pharmacopeial standards.
tags: FTIR, infrared spectroscopy, molecular identification, polymer, pharmaceutical, ATR, chemical analysis, quality control

name: Gas Chromatograph - Mass Spectrometer (GC-MS)
short description: Gas chromatography, mass spectrometry (GC, MS) combines gas chromatographic separation with mass spectrometric detection to identify and quantify volatile and semi, volatile organic compounds. It is widely used in environmental, forensic, food safety, and chemical analysis.
typical applications: Environmental pollutant detection (pesticides, VOCs), Drug and toxicology screening in forensics, Food safety testing (flavor, contaminant analysis), Petrochemical and fuel composition analysis, Metabolomics profiling of volatile metabolites
research-oriented use: 1. Screening environmental water samples for trace, level pesticide residues using triple, quadrupole GC, MS/MS. 2. Identifying volatile organic metabolites in plant tissues for metabolomics studies.
tags: GC, MS, mass spectrometry, chromatography, volatile organic compounds, environmental analysis, forensics, food safety, metabolomics

name: High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph (HPLC)
short description: High, performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) is an analytical technique that separates, identifies, and quantifies compounds in liquid samples under high pressure. It offers high resolution and sensitivity and is a mainstay of analytical chemistry across pharmaceutical, environmental, food, and clinical laboratories.
typical applications: Pharmaceutical drug purity testing and formulation analysis, Metabolite identification in clinical research, Food additive and pesticide residue quantification, Environmental water and soil contamination detection, Protein and peptide separation in biopharmaceutics
research-oriented use: 1. Quantifying catechin content in tea leaf extracts for food quality assessment using reversed, phase HPLC. 2. Monitoring drug dissolution profiles for pharmaceutical quality control under pharmacopeial methods.
tags: HPLC, liquid chromatography, separation, pharmaceutical, food safety, environmental analysis, quality control, UHPLC

name: UV-Vis Spectrophotometer
short description: Ultraviolet–visible spectrophotometry (UV–Vis or UV, VIS) refers to absorption spectroscopy or reflectance spectroscopy in part of the ultraviolet and the full, adjacent visible regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. Being relatively inexpensive and easily implemented, this methodology is widely used in diverse applied and fundamental applications. The only requirement is that the sample absorb in the UV–Vis region, i.e. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Lead Iodide Perovskite Sensitized All, Solid, State Submicron Thin Film Mesoscopic Solar Cell with Efficiency Exceeding 9% (Scientific Reports, 2012), Absorption spectral slopes and slope ratios as indicators of molecular weight, source, and photobleaching of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (Limnology and Oceanography, 2008), Effects of crystallization and dopant concentration on the emission behavior of TiO2:Eu nanophosphors (Nanoscale Research Letters, 2012), Synthesis and crystal chemistry of the hybrid perovskite (CH3NH3)PbI3 for solid, state sensitised solar cell applications (Journal of Materials Chemistry A, 2013), Natural deep eutectic solvents as new potential media for green technology (Analytica Chimica Acta, 2013)
research-oriented use: 1. Diverse applied and fundamental applications using UV, Vis Spectrophotometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating UV, Vis Spectrophotometer into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: X-ray Diffractometer (XRD)
short description: X, ray crystallography is the experimental science of determining the atomic and molecular structure of a crystal, in which the crystalline structure causes a beam of incident X, rays to diffract in specific directions. By measuring the angles and intensities of the X, ray diffraction, a crystallographer can produce a three, dimensional picture of the density of electrons within the crystal and the positions of the atoms, as well as their chemical bonds, crystallographic disorder, and other information. X, ray crystallography has been fundamental in the development of many scientific fields. Equipment at University in National Oceanography Centre Campus (UK).
typical applications: Single, crystal structure validation with the programPLATON (Journal of Applied Crystallography, 2003), The Cambridge Structural Database (Acta Crystallographica Section B Structural Science Crystal Engineering and Materials, 2016), An Empirical Method for Estimating the Degree of Crystallinity of Native Cellulose Using the X, Ray Diffractometer (Textile Research Journal, 1959), Lead Iodide Perovskite Sensitized All, Solid, State Submicron Thin Film Mesoscopic Solar Cell with Efficiency Exceeding 9% (Scientific Reports, 2012), An empirical method for correcting diffractometer data for absorption effects (Acta Crystallographica Section A Foundations of Crystallography, 1983)
research-oriented use: 1. Determining the crystal structure and phase composition of newly synthesized materials using X, ray Diffractometer (XRD) for structural characterization in materials research. 2. Assessing residual stress and crystallite size in thin, film coatings with X, ray Diffractometer (XRD) for engineering and surface science studies.

name: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectrometer (NMR)
short description: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a non, destructive analytical technique that provides detailed information about molecular structure, dynamics, and chemical environment. NMR exploits the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei and is indispensable in organic chemistry, biochemistry, and pharmaceutical research.
typical applications: Structure elucidation and verification of organic molecules, Protein structure determination in solution, Metabolomics profiling of complex biological mixtures, Reaction monitoring and kinetics studies, Quality control and purity assessment of chemicals
research-oriented use: 1. Determining the three, dimensional structure of a protein, ligand complex in solution using multidimensional NMR. 2. Quantitative NMR (qNMR) for purity determination of pharmaceutical reference standards without external calibrants.
tags: NMR, nuclear magnetic resonance, spectroscopy, organic chemistry, protein structure, metabolomics, molecular structure, quantitative analysis

name: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer (ICP-MS)
short description: ICP, MS is a highly sensitive analytical technique for measuring trace and ultra, trace elemental concentrations in a wide range of sample types. It uses an inductively coupled plasma to ionize sample atoms, which are then separated and detected by a mass spectrometer.
typical applications: Trace element analysis in environmental water and soil samples, Heavy metal contaminant testing in food and beverages, Elemental impurity analysis in pharmaceuticals (ICH Q3D), Geochemistry and geochronology studies, Semiconductor material purity analysis
research-oriented use: 1. Quantifying ultra, trace levels of arsenic species in rice using LC, ICP, MS speciation analysis. 2. Uranium, lead geochronology dating of zircon crystals using laser ablation ICP, MS.
tags: ICP, MS, trace element analysis, mass spectrometry, environmental, geochemistry, pharmaceutical, heavy metals, elemental analysis

name: Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC)
short description: A differential scanning calorimeter measures heat flow associated with thermal transitions in materials as a function of temperature and time. DSC is widely used for characterizing melting, crystallization, glass transitions, curing, and oxidative stability of polymers, pharmaceuticals, foods, and other materials.
typical applications: Polymer melting point and glass transition temperature measurement, Pharmaceutical polymorph and purity screening, Curing kinetics of thermosets and adhesives, Oxidative stability and shelf, life prediction of food products, Battery material thermal stability assessment
research-oriented use: 1. Characterizing the glass transition temperature and crystallization behavior of novel biodegradable polymer blends. 2. Screening pharmaceutical excipient compatibility by detecting unexpected thermal events in drug, excipient mixtures.
tags: DSC, thermal analysis, calorimetry, glass transition, melting point, polymer, pharmaceutical, crystallization

name: Thermogravimetric Analyzer (TGA)
short description: Thermogravimetric analysis measures changes in sample weight as a function of temperature or time under a controlled atmosphere. TGA is used to study decomposition, oxidation, volatilization, and moisture content in a wide variety of materials including polymers, ceramics, pharmaceuticals, and composites.
typical applications: Thermal decomposition and stability profiling of polymers and composites, Moisture and volatile content determination, Compositional analysis of multi, component materials, Oxidative stability evaluation under controlled atmospheres, Ash and filler content measurement in composites
research-oriented use: 1. Determining the degradation temperature and char yield of novel flame, retardant polymer formulations under nitrogen atmosphere. 2. Quantifying moisture, volatile, and ash content in coal samples following ASTM standard methods.
tags: TGA, thermal analysis, thermogravimetry, decomposition, polymer, moisture, compositional analysis, stability

name: Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope (CLSM)
short description: A confocal laser scanning microscope uses a focused laser beam and pinhole aperture to produce high, resolution optical sections of thick specimens. By eliminating out, of, focus light, CLSM enables 3D reconstruction of fluorescently labeled biological samples with superior contrast.
typical applications: Fluorescence imaging of cells and tissues, 3D reconstruction of biological structures, Colocalization studies of multiple fluorescent labels, Live, cell imaging and time, lapse studies, Materials surface profiling and coating analysis
research-oriented use: 1. Tracking intracellular protein localization using multi, channel fluorescence and z, stack imaging in cancer cell lines. 2. Visualizing bacterial biofilm architecture on medical device surfaces using fluorescent staining and 3D confocal reconstruction.
tags: confocal microscopy, fluorescence, laser scanning, 3D imaging, cell biology, colocalization, live, cell imaging, biofilm

name: Atomic Force Microscope (AFM)
short description: An atomic force microscope measures surface topography and mechanical properties at the nanoscale by scanning a sharp tip over the sample surface. AFM operates in ambient conditions, liquids, or vacuum and can image both conductive and insulating materials with sub, nanometer vertical resolution.
typical applications: Nanoscale surface topography and roughness measurement, Mechanical property mapping (Young's modulus, adhesion), Characterization of thin films and coatings, Biological imaging of DNA, proteins, and cell membranes, Nanoindentation and force spectroscopy
research-oriented use: 1. Mapping the nanomechanical properties of polymer blend domains using PeakForce QNM AFM mode. 2. Imaging DNA origami nanostructures on mica substrates under fluid conditions.
tags: AFM, atomic force microscopy, surface topography, nanoscale, mechanical properties, thin film, nanoindentation, scanning probe

name: Raman Spectrometer
short description: Raman Laser Spectrometer (RLS) is a miniature Raman spectrometer  that is part of the science payload on board the European Space Agency's Rosalind Franklin rover, tasked to search for biosignatures and biomarkers on Mars. The rover is planned to be launched not earlier than 2028 and land on Mars in 2029. Raman spectroscopy is a technique employed to identify mineral phases produced by water, related processes. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Proposed minimum reporting standards for chemical analysis (Metabolomics, 2007), Rediscovering black phosphorus as an anisotropic layered material for optoelectronics and electronics (Nature Communications, 2014), Cellulose crystallinity index: measurement techniques and their impact on interpreting cellulase performance (Biotechnology for Biofuels, 2010), Ammonia as a case study for the spontaneous ionization of a simple hydrogen, bonded compound (Nature Communications, 2014), Effects of crystallization and dopant concentration on the emission behavior of TiO2:Eu nanophosphors (Nanoscale Research Letters, 2012)
research-oriented use: 1. Mineral phases produced by water, related processes using Raman Spectrometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Raman Spectrometer into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: X-ray Fluorescence Spectrometer (XRF)
short description: X, ray fluorescence (XRF) is the emission of characteristic "secondary" (or fluorescent) X, rays from a material that has been excited by being bombarded with high, energy X, rays or gamma rays. When a material is illuminated with high, energy X, rays, its atoms can become excited and emit their own unique, characteristic X, rays—a process similar to how a blacklight makes certain colors fluoresce. By measuring the energy and intensity of these emitted "secondary" X, rays, scientists can identify which elements are present in the sample and in what quantities. Equipment at University in National Oceanography Centre Campus (UK).
typical applications: A SARS, CoV, 2 protein interaction map reveals targets for drug repurposing (Nature, 2020), The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009), Cellulose crystallinity index: measurement techniques and their impact on interpreting cellulase performance (Biotechnology for Biofuels, 2010), SCIAMACHY: Mission Objectives and Measurement Modes (Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences, 1999), Hydrogels with tunable stress relaxation regulate stem cell fate and activity (Nature Materials, 2015)
research-oriented use: 1. Which elements are present in the sample and in what quantities using X, ray Fluorescence Spectrometer (XRF), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating X, ray Fluorescence Spectrometer (XRF) into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Rheometer
short description: A rheometer measures the flow and deformation behavior (rheology) of materials under applied forces. It quantifies viscosity, viscoelastic properties, and flow behavior of liquids, semi, solids, and soft materials, and is essential in formulation development and quality control.
typical applications: Viscosity measurement of paints, coatings, and adhesives, Viscoelastic characterization of polymer melts and solutions, Food texture and consistency analysis, Pharmaceutical gel and cream formulation optimization, Concrete and cement workability testing
research-oriented use: 1. Investigating the shear, thinning behavior and thixotropic recovery of injectable hydrogel formulations for biomedical applications. 2. Characterizing the viscoelastic properties of 3D, printing bio, inks for tissue engineering scaffolds.
tags: rheology, viscosity, viscoelastic, polymer, formulation, food science, coatings, quality control

name: Thermomechanical Analyzer (TMA)
short description: A thermomechanical analyzer measures dimensional changes (expansion, contraction, softening) of a material as a function of temperature under a controlled mechanical load. TMA determines coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE), softening points, and glass transition temperatures.
typical applications: Coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) measurement for PCB and electronic materials, Glass transition and softening point determination, Dimensional stability testing of films and fibers, Sintering and densification studies of ceramics, Composite laminate through, thickness expansion evaluation
research-oriented use: 1. Measuring the CTE mismatch between copper traces and FR, 4 substrates in PCB reliability studies. 2. Evaluating the dimensional stability of polymer films for flexible electronics under thermal cycling.
tags: TMA, thermal expansion, CTE, softening point, glass transition, dimensional stability, polymer, electronics

name: Dynamic Mechanical Analyzer (DMA)
short description: A dynamic mechanical analyzer measures the viscoelastic properties of materials as a function of temperature, frequency, and time by applying an oscillatory force. DMA is widely used to determine glass transition temperatures, damping behavior, and storage/loss moduli of polymers and composites.
typical applications: Glass transition temperature (Tg) determination via tan delta peaks, Frequency, dependent viscoelastic property mapping, Curing and cross, linking characterization of thermosets, Temperature, dependent stiffness of composites and elastomers, Creep and stress relaxation studies
research-oriented use: 1. Mapping the Tg shift in epoxy nanocomposites as a function of nanoparticle loading using multi, frequency DMA. 2. Evaluating the damping performance of vibration, absorbing elastomeric mounts under variable temperature.
tags: DMA, dynamic mechanical analysis, viscoelastic, glass transition, modulus, polymer, composite, damping

name: Optical Profilometer
short description: Sensofar is a technology company headquartered in Terrassa, Barcelona, founded in 2001 as a spin, off from the Center for Sensors, Instruments and Systems Development (CD6) at the Polytechnic University of Catalonia (UPC). The company develops non, contact optical 3D surface metrology systems based on confocal microscopy, interferometry, and focus variation. Its instruments are used in research laboratories, industrial quality inspection, and advanced manufacturing environments. Equipment at University of Nottingham.
typical applications: Flexible polymer transistors with high pressure sensitivity for application in electronic skin and health monitoring (Nature Communications, 2013), Real surface area measurements in electrochemistry (Pure and Applied Chemistry, 1991), Low, threshold amplified spontaneous emission and lasing from colloidal nanocrystals of caesium lead halide perovskites (Nature Communications, 2015), Engineering triangular carbon quantum dots with unprecedented narrow bandwidth emission for multicolored LEDs (Nature Communications, 2018), Mechanical behavior of additive manufactured, powder, bed laser, fused materials (Materials Science and Engineering A, 2015)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using Optical Profilometer to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with Optical Profilometer for materials science research.

name: Fluorescence Spectrophotometer
short description: Spectrophotometry is a branch of electromagnetic spectroscopy concerned with the quantitative measurement of the reflection or transmission properties of a material as a function of wavelength. Spectrophotometry uses photometers, known as spectrophotometers, that can measure the intensity of a light beam at different wavelengths. Although spectrophotometry is most commonly applied to ultraviolet, visible, and infrared radiation, modern spectrophotometers can interrogate wide swaths of the electromagnetic spectrum, including x, ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, or microwave wavelengths. Equipment at University in Southampton General Hospital (UK).
typical applications: Loop, mediated isothermal amplification of DNA (Nucleic Acids Research, 2000), Changes in Gut Microbiota Control Metabolic Endotoxemia, Induced Inflammation in High, Fat Diet–Induced Obesity and Diabetes in Mice (Diabetes, 2008), The colorimetric estimation of formaldehyde by means of the Hantzsch reaction (Biochemical Journal, 1953), How to measure and predict the molar absorption coefficient of a protein (Protein Science, 1995), Characterization of spike glycoprotein of SARS, CoV, 2 on virus entry and its immune cross, reactivity with SARS, CoV (Nature Communications, 2020)
research-oriented use: 1. The intensity of a light beam at different wavelengths using Fluorescence Spectrophotometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Fluorescence Spectrophotometer into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectrometer (EDS/EDX)
short description: Energy dispersive X, ray spectroscopy is a technique coupled to electron microscopes (SEM or TEM) that detects characteristic X, rays emitted from a sample under electron beam excitation. EDS provides rapid qualitative and semi, quantitative elemental analysis and mapping of sample composition at micro, and nano, scales.
typical applications: Elemental identification and quantification during SEM/TEM imaging, Elemental distribution mapping of cross, sections, Inclusion and precipitate composition analysis in metallurgy, Failure analysis and contamination identification, Geological mineral phase identification
research-oriented use: 1. Mapping the elemental distribution of catalyst nanoparticles dispersed on a support material using SEM, EDS. 2. Identifying the composition of corrosion products on pipeline steel using cross, sectional EDS mapping.
tags: EDS, EDX, elemental analysis, X, ray spectroscopy, SEM, TEM, microanalysis, composition mapping

name: Gel Permeation Chromatograph (GPC/SEC)
short description: Gel permeation chromatography (GPC), also known as size exclusion chromatography (SEC), separates molecules based on their hydrodynamic volume (size) in solution. It is the primary technique for determining molecular weight distribution and polydispersity of synthetic polymers and biopolymers.
typical applications: Molecular weight and polydispersity determination of polymers, Protein aggregate and monomer separation in biopharmaceutics, Degradation and stability studies of polymer materials, Natural polymer (starch, cellulose) characterization, Quality control of polymer production batches
research-oriented use: 1. Monitoring the molecular weight degradation of biodegradable polyesters during accelerated aging studies. 2. Analyzing monoclonal antibody aggregates and fragments using SEC with multi, angle light scattering detection.
tags: GPC, SEC, size exclusion chromatography, molecular weight, polymer, biopharmaceutical, polydispersity, protein aggregation

name: X-ray Photoelectron Spectrometer (XPS)
short description: X, ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is a surface, sensitive quantitative spectroscopic technique that measures the very topmost 50–60 atoms, 5–10 nm of any surface. It belongs to the family of photoemission spectroscopies in which electron population spectra are obtained by irradiating a material with a beam of X, rays. XPS is based on the photoelectric effect that can identify the elements that exist within a material (elemental composition) or are covering its surface, as well as their chemical state, and the overall electronic structure and density of the electronic states in the material. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC (Journal of Instrumentation, 2008), The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009), Exfoliation of layered double hydroxides for enhanced oxygen evolution catalysis (Nature Communications, 2014), Ti3C2 MXene co, catalyst on metal sulfide photo, absorbers for enhanced visible, light photocatalytic hydrogen production (Nature Communications, 2017), The LHCb Detector at the LHC (Journal of Instrumentation, 2008)
research-oriented use: 1. The very topmost 50–60 atoms using X, ray Photoelectron Spectrometer (XPS), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. The elements that exist within a material (elemental composition) or are covering its surface with X, ray Photoelectron Spectrometer (XPS) for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: Focused Ion Beam (FIB) System
short description: Focused ion beam, also known as FIB, is a technique used particularly in the semiconductor industry, materials science and increasingly in the biological field for site, specific analysis, deposition, and ablation of materials. A FIB setup is a scientific instrument that resembles a scanning electron microscope (SEM). However, while the SEM uses a focused beam of electrons to image the sample in the chamber, a FIB setup uses a focused beam of ions instead. Equipment at Royal Holloway, University of London.
typical applications: Quantum cryptography (Reviews of Modern Physics, 2002), Advanced capabilities for materials modelling with Quantum ESPRESSO (Journal of Physics Condensed Matter, 2017), Macromolecular structure determination using X, rays, neutrons and electrons: recent developments in Phenix (Acta Crystallographica Section D Structural Biology, 2019), Cavity optomechanics (Reviews of Modern Physics, 2014), Stochastic resonance (Reviews of Modern Physics, 1998)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using Focused Ion Beam (FIB) System to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with Focused Ion Beam (FIB) System for materials science research.

name: Sputter Coater
short description: A sputter coater deposits a thin conductive layer (typically gold, platinum, or carbon) onto non, conductive samples to prepare them for SEM observation. Sputtering uses energized gas ions to eject target atoms, which then coat the sample uniformly at nanometer, scale thickness.
typical applications: SEM sample preparation for non, conductive samples (polymers, ceramics, biological tissue), Thin conductive film deposition for electron microscopy, Surface modification with metallic or carbon coatings, Anti, charging layer application for high, resolution SEM imaging
research-oriented use: 1. Coating polymer nanofiber scaffolds with a thin gold, palladium layer for high, resolution SEM morphological characterization. 2. Applying carbon coatings to geological thin sections for quantitative EDS microanalysis avoiding metallic peak interference.
tags: sputter coater, SEM preparation, thin film, conductive coating, gold, platinum, carbon, sample prep

name: Raman Microscope
short description: A Raman microscope combines a Raman spectrometer with an optical microscope, enabling spatially resolved chemical analysis at micrometer resolution. Confocal Raman imaging produces 2D and 3D chemical maps of heterogeneous samples with diffraction, limited spatial resolution.
typical applications: Spatially resolved chemical mapping of pharmaceutical tablets, Graphene and 2D material quality assessment and defect mapping, Stress/strain mapping in semiconductor devices, Mineral and inclusion identification in geological samples, Biological tissue and cell chemical imaging
research-oriented use: 1. Mapping the distribution of API and excipients in pharmaceutical tablet cross, sections using confocal Raman imaging. 2. Quantifying strain distribution in silicon, germanium heterostructures for semiconductor process development.
tags: Raman microscope, confocal Raman, chemical mapping, spatial resolution, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, imaging, spectroscopy

name: Stylus Profilometer
short description: Surface metrology is the measurement and characterization of surface topography, and is a branch of metrology. Surface primary form, surface fractality, and surface finish (including surface roughness) are the parameters most commonly associated with the field. Surface metrology is a fundamental measurement science critical across diverse manufacturing and engineering disciplines. Equipment at University College London.
typical applications: Atomic Force Microscope (Physical Review Letters, 1986), Durability of nanosized oxygen, barrier coatings on polymers (Progress in Materials Science, 2002), Hydrophilic surface modification of PDMS for droplet microfluidics using a simple, quick, and robust method via PVA deposition (Microsystems & Nanoengineering, 2017), Reconfigurable all, dielectric metalens with diffraction, limited performance (Nature Communications, 2021), The qPlus sensor, a powerful core for the atomic force microscope (Review of Scientific Instruments, 2019)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying Stylus Profilometer — surface metrology is the measurement and characterization of surface topography, and is a branch of metrology — to investigate research questions in physics and photonics. 2. Employing Stylus Profilometer as part of an integrated analytical workflow for industrial process optimization and scale, up.

name: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer
short description: A spectroscopic ellipsometer measures changes in polarization of light reflected from a sample to determine thin, film thickness, optical constants (n, k), and composition. It is a non, destructive, non, contact technique widely used in semiconductor, optics, and coatings research.
typical applications: Thin, film thickness and refractive index measurement, Optical constant (n, k) determination for multilayer stacks, Band gap estimation of semiconductors, In, situ monitoring of film growth (ALD, CVD), Polymer film swelling studies
research-oriented use: 1. Determining the thickness and optical constants of multi, layer perovskite solar cell stacks. 2. Monitoring in, situ swelling of hydrogel thin films upon solvent exposure.
tags: ellipsometry, thin film, optical constants, refractive index, thickness, non, destructive, semiconductor, coatings

name: Glovebox
short description: A glovebox (or glove box) is a sealed container that is designed to allow one to manipulate objects where a separate atmosphere is desired. Built into the sides of the glovebox are gloves arranged in such a way that the user can place their hands into the gloves and perform tasks inside the box without breaking containment. Part or all of the box is usually transparent to allow the user to see what is being manipulated. Equipment at University College London.
typical applications: Aggregation and morphology control enables multiple cases of high, efficiency polymer solar cells (Nature Communications, 2014), Solution, processed hybrid perovskite photodetectors with high detectivity (Nature Communications, 2014), Flexible polymer transistors with high pressure sensitivity for application in electronic skin and health monitoring (Nature Communications, 2013), A highly efficient polysulfide mediator for lithium–sulfur batteries (Nature Communications, 2015), Overcoming ultraviolet light instability of sensitized TiO2 with meso, superstructured organometal tri, halide perovskite solar cells (Nature Communications, 2013)
research-oriented use: 1. One to manipulate objects where a separate atmosphere is desired using Glovebox in a research setting, enabling systematic data collection for environmental science and monitoring studies. 2. The user to see what is being manipulated with Glovebox for quantitative analysis and reproducible experimental validation.

name: Single-Crystal X-ray Diffractometer
short description: A single, crystal X, ray diffractometer determines the full three, dimensional molecular structure of crystalline compounds by analyzing the diffraction pattern from a single crystal. It is the definitive technique for absolute structure determination in chemistry and mineralogy.
typical applications: Molecular structure determination of small molecules and coordination compounds, Absolute configuration assignment of chiral molecules, Crystal packing and intermolecular interaction analysis, Metal, organic framework (MOF) structure elucidation, Mineral and geological crystal characterization
research-oriented use: 1. The diffraction pattern from a single crystal using Single, Crystal X, ray Diffractometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Single, Crystal X, ray Diffractometer into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.
tags: single crystal XRD, crystallography, molecular structure, crystal structure, diffraction, absolute configuration, MOF, coordination chemistry

name: Thin-Film X-ray Diffractometer
short description: A thin, film X, ray diffractometer is optimized for analyzing thin films, epitaxial layers, and multilayer structures using grazing, incidence and high, resolution diffraction geometries. It provides crystallographic information on film texture, strain, thickness, and composition.
typical applications: Epitaxial layer quality assessment (rocking curves, reciprocal space maps), Thin, film phase identification and orientation analysis, Residual stress and strain measurement in coatings, Multilayer thickness determination via X, ray reflectivity (XRR), Texture and preferred orientation analysis
research-oriented use: 1. Measuring lattice mismatch and strain in epitaxial perovskite oxide thin films on SrTiO3 substrates. 2. Determining the thickness and roughness of sputtered multilayer stacks using X, ray reflectivity.
tags: thin film XRD, high, resolution XRD, epitaxy, strain, rocking curve, X, ray reflectivity, texture, multilayer

name: SQUID Magnetometer (MPMS)
short description: A SQUID magnetometer measures the magnetic moment of samples with extremely high sensitivity using a superconducting quantum interference device. The MPMS (Magnetic Property Measurement System) provides DC and AC susceptibility measurements over wide temperature and field ranges.
typical applications: DC magnetization and magnetic hysteresis measurements, AC susceptibility and magnetic relaxation studies, Curie/Néel temperature determination, Diamagnetic, paramagnetic, and ferromagnetic characterization, Thin, film and nanoparticle magnetic property studies
research-oriented use: 1. Measuring field, dependent magnetization of single, molecule magnets at low temperatures to determine anisotropy barriers. 2. Characterizing the magnetic phase transitions of multiferroic oxide thin films.
tags: SQUID, magnetometer, MPMS, magnetic properties, magnetization, susceptibility, superconducting, nanomagnetism

name: Physical Properties Measurement System (PPMS)
short description: The PPMS is a versatile cryogenic platform for measuring a wide range of physical properties including heat capacity, electrical transport, thermal conductivity, and magnetization. Its modular design supports multiple measurement options in a single 9 T, 2–400 K system.
typical applications: Heat capacity measurements (specific heat, Schottky anomalies), Electrical resistivity and Hall effect measurements, Thermal transport (Seebeck coefficient, thermal conductivity), Vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM), Torque magnetometry and AC transport
research-oriented use: 1. Measuring the temperature, dependent electrical resistivity and Hall coefficient of a topological semimetal. 2. Determining the specific heat anomaly at the superconducting transition of a novel material.
tags: PPMS, physical properties, heat capacity, resistivity, thermal transport, Seebeck, VSM, cryogenic, magnetism

name: Cryogenic Probe Station
short description: A cryogenic probe station enables electrical contacting and measurement of devices under vacuum at cryogenic temperatures using micromanipulated probes. It is crucial for low, temperature transport studies of semiconductors, superconductors, and 2D materials.
typical applications: Low, temperature electrical transport measurements, Semiconductor device characterization at variable temperatures, Superconducting transition temperature determination, 2D material and van der Waals heterostructure transport studies, Photocurrent mapping at cryogenic temperatures
research-oriented use: 1. Measuring the temperature, dependent resistance of a 2D material device to observe metal, insulator transitions. 2. Probing superconducting critical current and transition temperature of thin, film devices.
tags: probe station, cryogenic, low temperature, electrical transport, micromanipulator, semiconductor, superconductor, vacuum

name: Upright Optical Microscope
short description: An upright optical microscope uses visible light and a system of lenses to produce magnified images of sample surfaces in reflection or transmission mode. It is a fundamental tool for routine inspection, quality control, and sample screening in materials science and biology.
typical applications: Surface inspection and defect identification, Grain structure observation in metallography, Sample alignment and positioning for other instruments, Film and coating quality inspection, Biological tissue and cell observation (with transmitted light)
research-oriented use: 1. Screening thin, film samples for cracks, pinholes, and crystallization before more advanced characterization. 2. Imaging grain structures on polished and etched metal cross, sections for metallographic studies.
tags: optical microscope, light microscope, upright microscope, metallography, surface inspection, magnification, materials science

name: Thermal Evaporator
short description: A thermal evaporator deposits thin films of metals, dielectrics, or organic materials by resistive or electron, beam heating of source material under high vacuum. It is a core physical vapor deposition (PVD) technique used in device fabrication and materials research.
typical applications: Metal contact deposition for electronic devices (Au, Ag, Al, Cr), Organic layer deposition for OLEDs and organic solar cells, Dielectric thin film deposition (LiF, MoOx), Mirror and optical coating fabrication, Electrode deposition in micro/nanofabrication
research-oriented use: 1. Depositing Au top electrodes on organic thin, film transistors under high vacuum. 2. Co, evaporating organic donor and acceptor materials for bulk heterojunction solar cell active layers.
tags: thermal evaporation, PVD, thin film, metal deposition, organic electronics, vacuum, electrode, OLED

name: Spin Coater
short description: A spin coater deposits uniform thin films by dispensing a solution onto a rapidly spinning substrate. Centrifugal force spreads the solution evenly, and subsequent solvent evaporation leaves a controlled, thickness solid film. It is the most common lab, scale coating technique for photoresists, polymers, and functional thin films.
typical applications: Photoresist coating for lithography, Organic semiconductor and perovskite thin, film deposition, Polymer thin, film preparation for optical and electronic applications, Sol, gel and nanoparticle film deposition, Surface functionalization layer coating
research-oriented use: 1. Optimizing spin coating parameters for uniform perovskite absorber layers in solar cell fabrication. 2. Coating photoresist layers of precise thickness for electron, beam lithography patterning.
tags: spin coating, thin film, photoresist, deposition, organic electronics, perovskite, polymer film, lithography

name: Solar Simulator
short description: A solar simulator provides standardized illumination (typically AM1.5G, 100 mW/cm²) to mimic sunlight for photovoltaic device testing. It is used together with a sourcemeter for current, voltage (J, V) characterization and efficiency determination of solar cells.
typical applications: Solar cell J, V characterization and efficiency measurement, Photostability and degradation testing under simulated sunlight, Photocatalysis and photoelectrochemistry experiments, Light soaking studies on perovskite and organic devices
research-oriented use: 1. Measuring the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells under standardized AM1.5G illumination. 2. Performing accelerated photostability studies of perovskite solar cells under continuous illumination.
tags: solar simulator, AM1.5G, photovoltaic, solar cell testing, efficiency, J, V curve, illumination, photostability

name: Low-Temperature Scanning Tunneling Microscope (LT-STM)
short description: A low, temperature scanning tunneling microscope images conducting surfaces with atomic resolution at cryogenic temperatures (down to 5 K) under ultra, high vacuum. Combined with non, contact AFM (Qplus sensor), it enables sub, molecular resolution imaging and spectroscopy of single molecules and surface structures.
typical applications: Atomic, resolution surface imaging under UHV at 5 K, Single, molecule imaging and manipulation, Scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) of electronic states, Non, contact AFM with sub, molecular resolution (Qplus), Surface reaction and self, assembly studies
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging the internal bond structure of a single organic molecule adsorbed on a metal surface using nc, AFM at 5 K. 2. Mapping the local density of states of a 2D material at atomic resolution using low, temperature STS.
tags: STM, scanning tunneling microscope, LT, STM, nc, AFM, Qplus, atomic resolution, UHV, surface science, single molecule

name: Variable-Temperature STM with XPS/UPS
short description: A variable, temperature scanning tunneling microscope (VT, STM) with integrated X, ray and UV photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS/UPS) enables combined surface imaging and electronic structure characterization under UHV. This multi, technique system provides both atomic, resolution imaging and chemical state information on the same sample.
typical applications: Variable, temperature surface imaging (RT to high temperature), In, situ XPS/UPS of surfaces prepared under UHV, Surface reaction monitoring with combined STM and spectroscopy, Electronic band structure and work function measurement (UPS), Thin, film growth studies with LEED and STM
research-oriented use: 1. Studying temperature, dependent surface reconstructions of a metal surface using VT, STM combined with LEED. 2. Correlating the chemical state (XPS) with surface morphology (STM) of an oxidized catalyst surface.
tags: VT, STM, scanning tunneling microscope, XPS, UPS, surface science, UHV, variable temperature, electronic structure, LEED

name: Atomic Layer Deposition System (ALD)
short description: An atomic layer deposition system deposits ultrathin films with atomic, level thickness control through sequential self, limiting surface reactions. ALD is essential for conformal coating of high, aspect, ratio structures and is widely used in semiconductor, energy, and catalysis research.
typical applications: Gate dielectric deposition in transistor fabrication (Al2O3, HfO2), Conformal coating of 3D nanostructures and porous materials, Passivation layers for solar cells and LEDs, Catalytic support coating and functionalization, Barrier layers for flexible electronics and packaging
research-oriented use: 1. Depositing ultrathin Al2O3 passivation layers on perovskite solar cells to improve stability. 2. Conformally coating high, aspect, ratio silicon nanowire arrays with TiO2 for photoelectrochemical water splitting.
tags: ALD, atomic layer deposition, thin film, conformal coating, gate dielectric, passivation, semiconductor, nanotechnology

name: Electron Beam Evaporator
short description: An electron beam evaporator deposits thin films of metals and dielectrics by using a focused electron beam to vaporize source material in a high, vacuum chamber. It offers high deposition rates, excellent film purity, and the ability to evaporate refractory materials that cannot be thermally evaporated.
typical applications: Metal thin, film deposition for microelectronics (Ti, Au, Pt, Al), Dielectric and optical coating deposition (SiO2, TiO2), Refractory metal deposition (W, Mo, Ta), Multi, layer stack fabrication for photonics and MEMS, Electrode deposition in nanofabrication workflows
research-oriented use: 1. Depositing Ti/Au contact pads for nanoscale device fabrication following electron, beam lithography. 2. Fabricating multi, layer dielectric mirrors for optical cavity experiments.
tags: e, beam evaporation, PVD, thin film, metal deposition, refractory, vacuum deposition, nanofabrication, semiconductor

name: Magnetron Sputter Deposition System
short description: A magnetron sputter deposition system deposits thin films by bombarding a target material with energized ions in a plasma, causing target atoms to eject and coat a substrate. DC magnetron sputtering is used for metals, while RF sputtering handles oxides and nitrides.
typical applications: Metal thin, film deposition (Au, Ag, Cu, Ti, Cr), Oxide and nitride film deposition (ITO, SiN, Al2O3), Multilayer and alloy film fabrication, Hard coating deposition for wear resistance, Transparent conducting oxide (TCO) deposition
research-oriented use: 1. Depositing ITO transparent electrodes on glass substrates for organic LED fabrication. 2. Co, sputtering alloy thin films for combinatorial materials discovery studies.
tags: sputtering, magnetron, PVD, thin film, metal deposition, oxide, nitride, ITO, nanofabrication

name: Electron Beam Lithography System (EBL)
short description: An electron beam lithography system uses a focused electron beam to write custom nanoscale patterns directly into a resist, coated substrate without a mask. EBL provides sub, 10 nm patterning resolution and is essential for prototyping nanodevices, photonic structures, and MEMS.
typical applications: Nanoscale device patterning (transistors, sensors, nanowires), Photonic crystal and plasmonic structure fabrication, Custom mask and template fabrication, Directed self, assembly template patterning, Research, grade prototyping beyond optical lithography limits
research-oriented use: 1. Patterning sub, 100 nm nanowire channels for 2D material transport device fabrication. 2. Writing plasmonic nano, antenna arrays for surface, enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates.
tags: electron beam lithography, EBL, nanopatterning, nanofabrication, photonics, resist, MEMS, prototyping

name: Mask Aligner (UV Lithography)
short description: A mask aligner performs optical (UV) lithography by aligning a photomask to a resist, coated substrate and exposing it with UV light to transfer the mask pattern. It is a workhorse tool in microfabrication for producing patterns in the micrometer range and is available in standard UV and deep, UV configurations.
typical applications: Photoresist patterning for microfabrication, MEMS and microfluidic device fabrication, Thin, film electrode patterning, Multi, layer alignment for device fabrication, Back, side alignment for through, wafer processing
research-oriented use: 1. Patterning interdigitated electrode arrays on substrates for gas sensor fabrication using standard UV lithography. 2. Fabricating microfluidic channels in SU, 8 photoresist for lab, on, chip devices using deep, UV exposure.
tags: mask aligner, UV lithography, optical lithography, photoresist, microfabrication, MEMS, cleanroom, photomask

name: 3D Printer
short description: 3D printing, also called additive manufacturing, is the construction of a three, dimensional object from a CAD model or a digital 3D model. It can be done in a variety of processes in which material is deposited, joined or solidified under computer control, with the material being added together (e.g. plastics, liquids, or powder grains being fused), typically layer by layer. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: R: A Language and Environment for Statistical Computing (unknown, 2000), MOLSCRIPT: a program to produce both detailed and schematic plots of protein structures (Journal of Applied Crystallography, 1991), Avogadro: an advanced semantic chemical editor, visualization, and analysis platform (Journal of Cheminformatics, 2012), ESPript: analysis of multiple sequence alignments in PostScript. (Bioinformatics, 1999), A 3D bioprinting system to produce human, scale tissue constructs with structural integrity (Nature Biotechnology, 2016)
research-oriented use: 1. Fabricating patient, specific tissue scaffolds or prosthetic implants using 3D Printer for biomedical engineering research. 2. Prototyping complex geometries with controlled microstructure using 3D Printer for advanced manufacturing studies.

name: AFM
short description: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) or scanning force microscopy (SFM) is a very, high, resolution type of scanning probe microscopy (SPM), with demonstrated resolution on the order of fractions of a nanometer, more than 1000 times better than the optical diffraction limit. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles 2018 (MISEV2018): a position statement of the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles and update of the MISEV2014 guidelines (Journal of Extracellular Vesicles, 2018), brms: An R Package for Bayesian Multilevel Models Using Stan (Journal of Statistical Software, 2017), Bayesian Analysis of Radiocarbon Dates (Radiocarbon, 2009), WSXM: A software for scanning probe microscopy and a tool for nanotechnology (Review of Scientific Instruments, 2007), Folding DNA to create nanoscale shapes and patterns (Nature, 2006)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using AFM to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with AFM for materials science research.

name: ALD System
short description: Veeco Instruments Inc. is a global capital equipment supplier, headquartered in the U.S., that designs and builds processing systems used in semiconductor and  compound semiconductor manufacturing, data storage and scientific markets for applications such as advanced packaging, photonics, power electronics and display technologies. Veeco's processing system capabilities include laser annealing, photolithography, ion beam etch and deposition, metal organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD), wet wafer processing, molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), atomic layer deposition (ALD), physical vapor deposition (PVD), dicing and lapping, and gas and vapor delivery. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Pseudocapacitive oxide materials for high, rate electrochemical energy storage (Energy & Environmental Science, 2014), Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International guidelines for management of severe sepsis and septic shock: 2008 (Intensive Care Medicine, 2007), An overview of semiconductor photocatalysis (Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A Chemistry, 1997), The complete genome sequence of the gastric pathogen Helicobacter pylori (Nature, 1997), Automatic acquisition of hyponyms from large text corpora (unknown, 1992)
research-oriented use: 1. Semiconductor and compound semiconductor manufacturing using ALD System, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating ALD System into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Aquaculture System
short description: The Fishery Resources Monitoring System (FIRMS) is a partnership of intergovernmental fisheries organizations that share information on the global monitoring and management of marine fishery resources. Equipment at University of Sheffield.
typical applications: River plastic emissions to the world’s oceans (Nature Communications, 2017), Mangroves among the most carbon, rich forests in the tropics (Nature Geoscience, 2011), A Global Crisis for Seagrass Ecosystems (BioScience, 2006), Harmful algal blooms and eutrophication: Nutrient sources, composition, and consequences (Estuaries, 2002), Our evolving conceptual model of the coastal eutrophication problem (Marine Ecology Progress Series, 2001)
research-oriented use: 1. And management of marine fishery resources using Aquaculture System in a research setting, enabling systematic data collection for biological and life sciences studies. 2. Employing Aquaculture System as part of an integrated analytical workflow for field, based and in, situ measurement campaigns.

name: Atomic Absorption Spectrometer (AAS)
short description: Atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS) is an elemental analysis method for determining the concentration of metals in a given sample. The principle of AAS relies on the vaporization of metals within a sample when introduced to a flame. Every ground state metal absorbs light radiation (and excites) at a different wavelength. Equipment at University of Cambridge.
typical applications: Double, slit photoelectron interference in strong, field ionization of the neon dimer (Nature Communications, 2018), TheGaiamission (Astronomy and Astrophysics, 2016), Stochastic resonance (Reviews of Modern Physics, 1998), The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009), New handbook for standardised measurement of plant functional traits worldwide (Australian Journal of Botany, 2013)
research-oriented use: 1. Characterizing the chemical composition of novel materials by analyzing spectral signatures with Atomic Absorption Spectrometer (AAS) to identify functional groups and molecular structures. 2. Monitoring environmental pollutant concentrations in water or air samples using Atomic Absorption Spectrometer (AAS) for quantitative trace analysis in environmental science studies.

name: Auger Electron Spectrometer (AES)
short description: Auger electron spectroscopy (AES; pronounced [oʒe] in French) is a common analytical technique used specifically in the study of surfaces and, more generally, in the area of materials science. It is a form of electron spectroscopy that relies on the Auger effect, based on the analysis of energetic electrons emitted from an excited atom after a series of internal relaxation events. The Auger effect was discovered independently by both Lise Meitner and Pierre Auger in the 1920s. Equipment at University of Portsmouth.
typical applications: Femtosecond X, ray protein nanocrystallography (Nature, 2011), Fundamentals and advances in magnesium alloy corrosion (Progress in Materials Science, 2017), Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector (The Astrophysical Journal, 1998), Low, threshold amplified spontaneous emission and lasing from colloidal nanocrystals of caesium lead halide perovskites (Nature Communications, 2015), Electron, Ion Collider: The next QCD frontier (The European Physical Journal A, 2016)
research-oriented use: 1. Characterizing the chemical composition of novel materials by analyzing spectral signatures with Auger Electron Spectrometer (AES) to identify functional groups and molecular structures. 2. Monitoring environmental pollutant concentrations in water or air samples using Auger Electron Spectrometer (AES) for quantitative trace analysis in environmental science studies.

name: Autoclave / Sterilizer
short description: An autoclave is a machine used to carry out industrial and scientific processes requiring elevated temperature and pressure in relation to ambient pressure and temperature. Autoclaves are found in many medical settings, laboratories, and other places that need to ensure the sterility of an object. The autoclave was invented by Charles Chamberland in 1879, although a precursor known as the steam digester was created by Denis Papin in 1679. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts: a versatile cell system for transient gene expression analysis (Nature Protocols, 2007), PLAQUE FORMATION AND ISOLATION OF PURE LINES WITH POLIOMYELITIS VIRUSES (The Journal of Experimental Medicine, 1954), Reporting animal research: Explanation and elaboration for the ARRIVE guidelines 2.0 (PLoS Biology, 2020), Solar steam generation by heat localization (Nature Communications, 2014), Cytokinesis, block micronucleus cytome assay (Nature Protocols, 2007)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying Autoclave / Sterilizer — an autoclave is a machine used to carry out industrial and scientific processes requiring elevated temperature and pressure in relation to ambient pressure and temperature — to investigate research questions in biomedical and clinical research. 2. Employing Autoclave / Sterilizer as part of an integrated analytical workflow for industrial process optimization and scale, up.

name: Ball Mill
short description: The scientific method is an empirical method for acquiring knowledge through careful observation, rigorous skepticism, hypothesis testing, and experimental validation. Developed from ancient and medieval practices, it acknowledges that cognitive assumptions can distort the interpretation of the observation. The scientific method has characterized science since at least the 17th century. Equipment at University of Nottingham.
typical applications: Global, regional, and national incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability for 328 diseases and injuries for 195 countries, 1990–2016: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2016 (The Lancet, 2017), Anti de Sitter space and holography (Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics, 1998), An integrated map of genetic variation from 1,092 human genomes (Nature, 2012), A map of human genome variation from population, scale sequencing (Nature, 2010), Mechanical alloying and milling (Progress in Materials Science, 2001)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying Ball Mill — the scientific method is an empirical method for acquiring knowledge through careful observation, rigorous skepticism, hypothesis testing, and experimental validation — to investigate research questions in physics and photonics. 2. Employing Ball Mill as part of an integrated analytical workflow for comparative analysis and method validation in research.

name: BET Surface Area Analyzer
short description: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) is a private research university in Cleveland, Ohio, United States. It was federated in 1967 by a merger between Western Reserve University, founded in 1826 by the Presbyterian Church, and the Case Institute of Technology, founded in 1880. Case Western Reserve University comprises eight schools that offer more than 100 undergraduate programs and about 160 graduate and professional options across fields in STEM, medicine, arts, and the humanities. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: The natural history of insulin secretory dysfunction and insulin resistance in the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes mellitus (Journal of Clinical Investigation, 1999), Characterization of porous solids and powders: surface area, pore size, and density (Choice Reviews Online, 2005), Mechanism of free fatty acid, induced insulin resistance in humans. (Journal of Clinical Investigation, 1996), Hollow MnO2 as a tumor, microenvironment, responsive biodegradable nano, platform for combination therapy favoring antitumor immune responses (Nature Communications, 2017), Iron, based cathode catalyst with enhanced power density in polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells (Nature Communications, 2011)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying BET Surface Area Analyzer — case western reserve university (cwru) is a private research university in cleveland, ohio, united states — to investigate research questions in biomedical and clinical research. 2. Employing BET Surface Area Analyzer as part of an integrated analytical workflow for field, based and in, situ measurement campaigns.

name: Bioreactor / Fermenter
short description: Industrial fermentation is the intentional use of fermentation in manufacturing processes. In addition to the mass production of fermented foods and drinks, industrial fermentation has widespread applications in chemical industry. Commodity chemicals, such as acetic acid, citric acid, and ethanol are made by fermentation. Equipment at University of Portsmouth.
typical applications: High, level semi, synthetic production of the potent antimalarial artemisinin (Nature, 2013), Microbial Degradation of Petroleum Hydrocarbon Contaminants: An Overview (Biotechnology Research International, 2010), Bioconversion of lignocellulose: inhibitors and detoxification (Biotechnology for Biofuels, 2013), Micro‐algal biotechnology (FEBS Letters, 1988), Advances in plant growth, promoting bacterial inoculant technology: formulations and practical perspectives (1998–2013) (Plant and Soil, 2013)
research-oriented use: 1. Conducting controlled catalytic reactions in Bioreactor / Fermenter to screen catalyst performance and optimize reaction conditions for green chemistry research. 2. Studying reaction kinetics under varied temperature and pressure conditions using Bioreactor / Fermenter for chemical engineering process development.

name: Biosafety Cabinet / Fume Hood
short description: A fume hood (sometimes called a fume cupboard or fume closet, not to be confused with extractor hood) is a type of local exhaust ventilation device that is designed to prevent users from being exposed to hazardous fumes, vapors, and dusts. The device is an enclosure with a movable sash window on one side that traps and exhausts gases and particulates either out of the area (through a duct) or back into the room (through air filtration), and is most frequently used in laboratory settings. The first fume hoods, constructed from wood and glass, were developed in the early 1900s as a measure to protect individuals from harmful gaseous reaction by, products. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: Electrical stimulation systems for cardiac tissue engineering (Nature Protocols, 2009), Quantification of SARS, CoV, 2 neutralizing antibody by wild, type plaque reduction neutralization, microneutralization and pseudotyped virus neutralization assays (Nature Protocols, 2021), Development of a Laboratory, safe and Low, cost Detection Protocol for SARS, CoV, 2 of the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID, 19) (Experimental Neurobiology, 2020), Effectiveness of Three Decontamination Treatments against Influenza Virus Applied to Filtering Facepiece Respirators (The Annals of Occupational Hygiene, 2011), Characterization and Control of Airborne Particles Emitted During Production of Epoxy/Carbon Nanotube Nanocomposites (Journal of Occupational and Environmental Hygiene, 2011)
research-oriented use: 1. Laboratory settings using Biosafety Cabinet / Fume Hood in a research setting, enabling systematic data collection for chemical and molecular sciences studies. 2. To protect individuals from harmful gaseous reaction by, products with Biosafety Cabinet / Fume Hood for quantitative analysis and reproducible experimental validation.

name: Cell Sorter
short description: Cell sorting is the process through which a particular cell type is separated from others contained in a sample on the basis of its physical or biological properties, such as size, morphological parameters, viability and both extracellular and intracellular protein expression. The homogeneous cell population obtained after sorting can be used for a variety of applications including research, diagnosis, and therapy. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: A short history ofSHELX (Acta Crystallographica Section A Foundations of Crystallography, 2007), NIH Image to ImageJ: 25 years of image analysis (Nature Methods, 2012), Coot: model, building tools for molecular graphics (Acta Crystallographica Section D Biological Crystallography, 2004), Clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (Neurology, 1984), featureCounts: an efficient general purpose program for assigning sequence reads to genomic features (Bioinformatics, 2013)
research-oriented use: 1. A variety of applications including research using Cell Sorter, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Cell Sorter into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Ceramic Kiln
short description: Pottery is the process and the products of forming vessels and other objects with clay and other raw materials, which are fired at high temperatures to give them a hard and durable form. The place where such wares are made by a potter is also called a pottery (plural potteries). The definition of pottery, used by the ASTM International, is "all fired ceramic wares that contain clay when formed, except technical, structural, and refractory products". Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: The role of hydrogen and fuel cells in the global energy system (Energy & Environmental Science, 2018), A technology‐based global inventory of black and organic carbon emissions from combustion (Journal of Geophysical Research Atmospheres, 2004), Geopolymers and Related Alkali, Activated Materials (Annual Review of Materials Research, 2014), New horizons for inorganic solid state ion conductors (Energy & Environmental Science, 2018), Joint Optimization of Radio and Computational Resources for Multicell Mobile, Edge Computing (IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks, 2015)
research-oriented use: 1. Mapping nanoscale surface morphology and mechanical properties of biomaterials using Ceramic Kiln for nanotechnology research. 2. Measuring local electrical or magnetic properties at the nanoscale with Ceramic Kiln for condensed, matter physics studies.

name: Circular Dichroism Spectrometer (CD)
short description: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) is the differential absorption of left and right circularly polarized (LCP and RCP) light, induced in a sample by a strong magnetic field oriented parallel to the direction of light propagation. MCD measurements can detect transitions which are too weak to be seen in conventional optical absorption spectra, and it can be used to distinguish between overlapping transitions. Paramagnetic systems are common analytes, as their near, degenerate magnetic sublevels provide strong MCD intensity that varies with both field strength and sample temperature. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Electrical control of neutral and charged excitons in a monolayer semiconductor (Nature Communications, 2013), Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman Spectroscopy (Scientific Reports, 2013), Inhibition of SARS, CoV, 2 (previously 2019, nCoV) infection by a highly potent pan, coronavirus fusion inhibitor targeting its spike protein that harbors a high capacity to mediate membrane fusion (Cell Research, 2020), Redox, responsive self, healing materials formed from host–guest polymers (Nature Communications, 2011), G, quadruplexes in promoters throughout the human genome (Nucleic Acids Research, 2006)
research-oriented use: 1. Distinguish between overlapping transitions using Circular Dichroism Spectrometer (CD), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Transitions which are too weak to be seen in conventional optical absorption spectra with Circular Dichroism Spectrometer (CD) for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: CNC Machine
short description: A machine shop or engineering workshop is a room, building, or company where machining, a form of subtractive manufacturing, is done. In a machine shop, machinists use machine tools and cutting tools to make parts, usually of metal or plastic (but sometimes of other materials such as glass or wood). A machine shop can be a small business (such as a job shop) or a portion of a factory, whether a toolroom or a production area for manufacturing. Equipment at Queen's University Belfast.
typical applications: Design for Additive Manufacturing: Trends, opportunities, considerations, and constraints (CIRP Annals, 2016), Manufacturing Automation: Metal Cutting Mechanics, Machine Tool Vibrations, and CNC Design (Applied Mechanics Reviews, 2001), A terrestrial planet candidate in a temperate orbit around Proxima Centauri (Nature, 2016), Industry 4.0 Concept: Background and Overview (International Journal of Interactive Mobile Technologies (iJIM), 2017), Exploratory graph analysis: A new approach for estimating the number of dimensions in psychological research (PLoS ONE, 2017)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying CNC Machine — a machine shop or engineering workshop is a room, building, or company where machining, a form of subtractive manufacturing, is done — to investigate research questions in materials science and engineering. 2. Employing CNC Machine as part of an integrated analytical workflow for industrial process optimization and scale, up.

name: Confocal Microscope (CLSM)
short description: Confocal microscopy, most frequently confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) or laser scanning confocal microscopy (LSCM), is an optical imaging technique for increasing optical resolution and contrast of a micrograph by means of using a spatial pinhole to block out, of, focus light in image formation. Capturing multiple two, dimensional images at different depths in a sample enables the reconstruction of three, dimensional structures (a process known as optical sectioning) within an object. This technique is used extensively in the scientific and industrial communities and typical applications are in life sciences, semiconductor inspection and materials science. Equipment at University in Southampton General Hospital (UK).
typical applications: A pneumonia outbreak associated with a new coronavirus of probable bat origin (Nature, 2020), Spatial reconstruction of single, cell gene expression data (Nature Biotechnology, 2015), Neurogenesis in the adult human hippocampus (Nature Medicine, 1998), ImageJ2: ImageJ for the next generation of scientific image data (BMC Bioinformatics, 2017), CellProfiler: image analysis software for identifying and quantifying cell phenotypes (Genome biology, 2006)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using Confocal Microscope (CLSM) to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with Confocal Microscope (CLSM) for materials science research.

name: Contact Angle Goniometer
short description: The law of constancy of interfacial angles (German: Das Gesetz der Winkelkonstanz; French: Loi de constance des angles) is an empirical law in the fields of crystallography and mineralogy concerning the shape, or morphology, of crystals. The law states that the angles between adjacent corresponding faces of crystals of a particular substance are always constant despite the different shapes, sizes, and mode of growth of crystals. The law is also named the first law of crystallography or Steno's law. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: Measurement of lower extremity kinematics during level walking (Journal of Orthopaedic Research®, 1990), Characterization and Distribution of Water, repellent, Self, cleaning Plant Surfaces (Annals of Botany, 1997), Stable lithium electrodeposition in liquid and nanoporous solid electrolytes (Nature Materials, 2014), An ultra, sensitive resistive pressure sensor based on hollow, sphere microstructure induced elasticity in conducting polymer film (Nature Communications, 2014), Characterization of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) Properties for Biomedical Micro/Nanosystems (Biomedical Microdevices, 2005)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying Contact Angle Goniometer — the law of constancy of interfacial angles (german: das gesetz der winkelkonstanz; french: loi de constance des angles) is an empirical law in the fields of crystallography and mineralogy concerning the shape, or morphology, of crystals — to investigate research questions in materials science and engineering. 2. Employing Contact Angle Goniometer as part of an integrated analytical workflow for field, based and in, situ measurement campaigns.

name: Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM)
short description: A coordinate, measuring machine (CMM) is a device that measures the geometry of physical objects by sensing discrete points on the surface of the object with a probe. Various types of probes are used in CMMs, the most common being mechanical and laser sensors, though optical and white light sensors do exist. Depending on the machine, the probe position may be manually controlled by an operator, or it may be computer controlled. Equipment at University of Strathclyde.
typical applications: SciPy 1.0: fundamental algorithms for scientific computing in Python (Nature Methods, 2020), QUANTUM ESPRESSO: a modular and open, source software project for quantum simulations of materials (Journal of Physics Condensed Matter, 2009), Initial sequencing and analysis of the human genome (Nature, 2001), phyloseq: An R Package for Reproducible Interactive Analysis and Graphics of Microbiome Census Data (PLoS ONE, 2013), Development and Distortion of Malaysian Public, Private Partnerships: Patronage, Privatised Profits and Pitfalls DOI: 10.1111/j.1467, 8500.2009.00655.x (Intellectum (Universidad de La Sabana), 2010)
research-oriented use: 1. CMMs, the most common being mechanical and laser sensors using Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Coulter Counter / Cell Counter
short description: Celloscope automated cell counter was developed in the 1950s for enumeration of erythrocytes, leukocytes, and thrombocytes in blood samples. Together with the Coulter counter, the Celloscope analyzer can be considered one of the predecessors of today's automated hematology analyzers, as the principle of the electrical impedance method is still utilized in cell counters installed in clinical laboratories around the world. Equipment at University in Southampton General Hospital (UK).
typical applications: Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of single cells (Nature Communications, 2017), CellProfiler: image analysis software for identifying and quantifying cell phenotypes (Genome biology, 2006), Biological Defense Mechanisms.
