THE PRODUCTION BY LEUKOCYTES OF SUPEROXIDE, A POTENTIAL BACTERICIDAL AGENT (Journal of Clinical Investigation, 1973), The polycomb group protein EZH2 is involved in progression of prostate cancer (Nature, 2002), Nile red: a selective fluorescent stain for intracellular lipid droplets. (The Journal of Cell Biology, 1985)
research-oriented use: 1. Automating high, throughput compound screening using Coulter Counter / Cell Counter for drug discovery campaigns. 2. Deploying Coulter Counter / Cell Counter for reproducible sample preparation in large, scale genomics or proteomics studies.

name: Creep Testing Machine
short description: A creep, testing machine measures the alteration of a material after it has undergone stresses. Engineers use Creep machines to determine the stability and behaviour of a material when put through ordinary stresses. They determine how much strain (load) an object can handle under pressure, so engineers and researchers are able to determine what materials to use. Equipment at University of Nottingham.
typical applications: Nickel, Based Superalloys for Advanced Turbine Engines: Chemistry, Microstructure and Properties (Journal of Propulsion and Power, 2006), Physics of thin, film ferroelectric oxides (Reviews of Modern Physics, 2005), A field study of the software design process for large systems (Communications of the ACM, 1988), Additive manufacturing: scientific and technological challenges, market uptake and opportunities (Materials Today, 2017), Fundamentals and advances in magnesium alloy corrosion (Progress in Materials Science, 2017)
research-oriented use: 1. The alteration of a material after it has undergone stresses using Creep Testing Machine in a research setting, enabling systematic data collection for materials science and engineering studies. 2. The stability and behaviour of a material when put through ordinary stresses with Creep Testing Machine for quantitative analysis and reproducible experimental validation.

name: Critical Point Dryer
short description: A pH meter is a scientific instrument that measures the hydrogen, ion activity in water, based solutions, indicating its acidity or alkalinity expressed as pH. The pH meter measures the difference in electrical potential between a pH electrode and a reference electrode, and so the pH meter is sometimes referred to as a "potentiometric pH meter". The difference in electrical potential relates to the acidity or pH of the solution. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: Older Adults' Reasons for Using Technology while Aging in Place (Gerontology, 2015), NCEP–DOE AMIP, II Reanalysis (R, 2) (Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 2002), River plastic emissions to the world’s oceans (Nature Communications, 2017), The role of hydrogen and fuel cells in the global energy system (Energy & Environmental Science, 2018), The myth of language universals: Language diversity and its importance for cognitive science (Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 2009)
research-oriented use: 1. The hydrogen, ion activity in water, based solutions using Critical Point Dryer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. The difference in electrical potential between a pH electrode and a reference electrode with Critical Point Dryer for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: Cryo-Electron Microscope (Cryo-EM)
short description: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo, EM) is a transmission electron microscopy technique applied to samples cooled to cryogenic temperatures. Developed in the 1970s, advances in detector technology and software allow biomolecular structures to be imaged at near, atomic resolution. The approach has become a popular alternative to X, ray crystallography or NMR spectroscopy in structural biology. Equipment at University of Cambridge.
typical applications: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles 2018 (MISEV2018): a position statement of the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles and update of the MISEV2014 guidelines (Journal of Extracellular Vesicles, 2018), cryoSPARC: algorithms for rapid unsupervised cryo, EM structure determination (Nature Methods, 2017), Double, slit photoelectron interference in strong, field ionization of the neon dimer (Nature Communications, 2018), Convergent antibody responses to SARS, CoV, 2 in convalescent individuals (Nature, 2020), Cross, neutralization of SARS, CoV, 2 by a human monoclonal SARS, CoV antibody (Nature, 2020)
research-oriented use: 1. Biomolecular structures to be imaged at near, atomic resolution using Cryo, Electron Microscope (Cryo, EM), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Cryo, Electron Microscope (Cryo, EM) into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Cryogenics System
short description: Titan Submarine is a proposed unmanned NASA submarine probe that will visit Saturn's largest moon Titan, and will explore either Kraken Mare or Ligeia Mare, two of Titan's lakes. The concept was proposed by Steven Oleson, Ralph Lorenz, and Micheal Paul, technical experts at the Glenn Research Center in Ohio. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger (Physical Review Letters, 2016), Double, slit photoelectron interference in strong, field ionization of the neon dimer (Nature Communications, 2018), Folding DNA to create nanoscale shapes and patterns (Nature, 2006), TheGaiamission (Astronomy and Astrophysics, 2016), Quantum computation with quantum dots (Physical Review A, 1998)
research-oriented use: 1. Mapping nanoscale surface morphology and mechanical properties of biomaterials using Cryogenics System for nanotechnology research. 2. Measuring local electrical or magnetic properties at the nanoscale with Cryogenics System for condensed, matter physics studies.

name: Cryostat
short description: A cryostat (from cryo meaning cold and stat meaning stable) is a device used to maintain low cryogenic temperatures of samples or devices mounted within the cryostat. Low temperatures may be maintained within a cryostat by using various refrigeration methods, most commonly using cryogenic fluid bath such as liquid helium. Hence it is usually assembled into a vessel, similar in construction to a vacuum flask or Dewar. Equipment at University of St Andrews.
typical applications: Re, epithelialization and immune cell behaviour in an ex vivo human skin model (Scientific Reports, 2020), Double, slit photoelectron interference in strong, field ionization of the neon dimer (Nature Communications, 2018), Culture of Human Endothelial Cells Derived from Umbilical Veins. IDENTIFICATION BY MORPHOLOGIC AND IMMUNOLOGIC CRITERIA (Journal of Clinical Investigation, 1973), The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC (Journal of Instrumentation, 2008), Analysis of the Human Tissue, specific Expression by Genome, wide Integration of Transcriptomics and Antibody, based Proteomics (Molecular & Cellular Proteomics, 2013)
research-oriented use: 1. Cryostats used in MRI machines are designed to hold a cryogen, typically helium, in a liquid state with minimal evaporation (boil, off). 2. The liquid helium bath is designed to keep the superconducting magnet's bobbin of superconductive wire in its superconductive state.

name: CT Scanner / Micro-CT
short description: In radiography, X, ray microtomography uses X, rays to create cross, sections of a physical object that can be used to recreate a virtual model (3D model) without destroying the original object. It is similar to tomography and X, ray computed tomography. The prefix micro, (symbol: μ) is used to indicate that the pixel sizes of the cross, sections are in the micrometre range. Equipment at University in Cambridge (UK).
typical applications: 2014 ESC Guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of aortic diseases (European Heart Journal, 2014), 2014 ESC Guidelines on the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism (European Heart Journal, 2014), Salience and Taxation: Theory and Evidence (American Economic Review, 2009), Limb proportions show developmental plasticity in response to embryo movement (Scientific Reports, 2017), An Optimization, Based Econometric Framework for the Evaluation of Monetary Policy (NBER Macroeconomics Annual, 1997)
research-oriented use: 1. Recreate a virtual model (3D model) without destroying the original object using CT Scanner / Micro, CT, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Indicate that the pixel sizes of the cross, sections are in the micrometre range with CT Scanner / Micro, CT for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: CVD System
short description: A synthetic diamond or laboratory, grown diamond (LGD), also called a lab, grown, laboratory, created, man, made, artisan, created, artificial, or cultured diamond, is a diamond that is produced in a controlled technological process, in contrast to a naturally formed diamond, which is created through geological processes and obtained by mining. Unlike diamond simulants (imitations of diamond made of superficially similar non, diamond materials), synthetic diamonds are composed of the same material as naturally formed diamonds—pure carbon crystallized in an isotropic 3D form—and have identical chemical and physical properties. The maximal size of synthetic diamonds has increased dramatically in the 21st century. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Harmonizing the Metabolic Syndrome (Circulation, 2009), 2013 ESH/ESC Guidelines for the management of arterial hypertension (European Heart Journal, 2013), 2018 ESC/ESH Guidelines for the management of arterial hypertension (European Heart Journal, 2018), World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2020), European Guidelines on cardiovascular disease prevention in clinical practice (version 2012): The Fifth Joint Task Force of the European Society of Cardiology and Other Societies on Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Clinical Practice (constituted by representatives of nine societies and by invited experts) * Developed with the special contribution of the European Association for Cardiovascular Prevention & Rehabilitation (EACPR) (European Heart Journal, 2012)
research-oriented use: 1. Applying CVD System — a synthetic diamond or laboratory, grown diamond (lgd), also called a lab, grown, laboratory, created, man, made, artisan, created, artificial, or cultured diamond, is a diamond that is produced in a controlled technological process, in contrast to a naturally formed diamond, which is created through geological processes and obtained by mining — to investigate research questions in chemical and molecular sciences. 2. Employing CVD System as part of an integrated analytical workflow for quality control and compliance verification.

name: Data Storage System
short description: A scientific instrument is a device or tool used for scientific purposes, including the study of both natural phenomena and theoretical research. Equipment at University in The Pirbright Institute (UK).
typical applications: R: A Language and Environment for Statistical Computing (unknown, 2000), Gradient, based learning applied to document recognition (Proceedings of the IEEE, 1998), Global cancer statistics (CA A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, 2011), XGBoost (unknown, 2016), SciPy 1.0: fundamental algorithms for scientific computing in Python (Nature Methods, 2020)
research-oriented use: 1. Scientific purposes using Data Storage System in a research setting, enabling systematic data collection for scientific research and analysis studies. 2. Employing Data Storage System as part of an integrated analytical workflow for comparative analysis and method validation in research.

name: Dicing Saw
short description: Veeco Instruments Inc. is a global capital equipment supplier, headquartered in the U.S., that designs and builds processing systems used in semiconductor and  compound semiconductor manufacturing, data storage and scientific markets for applications such as advanced packaging, photonics, power electronics and display technologies. Veeco's processing system capabilities include laser annealing, photolithography, ion beam etch and deposition, metal organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD), wet wafer processing, molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), atomic layer deposition (ALD), physical vapor deposition (PVD), dicing and lapping, and gas and vapor delivery. Equipment at University College London.
typical applications: The qualitative content analysis process (Journal of Advanced Nursing, 2008), Highly Specific Gene Silencing by Artificial MicroRNAs in Arabidopsis (The Plant Cell, 2006), A decade of Predictions in Ungauged Basins (PUB)—a review (Hydrological Sciences Journal, 2013), Integrated photonics on thin, film lithium niobate (Advances in Optics and Photonics, 2021), Characterization of microRNA expression profiles in normal human tissues (BMC Genomics, 2007)
research-oriented use: 1. Semiconductor and compound semiconductor manufacturing using Dicing Saw, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Dicing Saw into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Digital Microscope
short description: A microscope (from Ancient Greek  μικρός (mikrós) 'small' and  σκοπέω (skopéō) 'to look (at); examine, inspect') is a laboratory instrument used to examine objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye. Microscopy is the science of investigating small objects and structures using a microscope. Microscopic means being invisible to the eye unless aided by a microscope. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: NIH Image to ImageJ: 25 years of image analysis (Nature Methods, 2012), Copper, Zinc Superoxide Dismutase (SOD1) Is Released by Microglial Cells and Confers Neuroprotection against 6, OHDA Neurotoxicity (Neurosignals, 2012), Lead Iodide Perovskite Sensitized All, Solid, State Submicron Thin Film Mesoscopic Solar Cell with Efficiency Exceeding 9% (Scientific Reports, 2012), WSXM: A software for scanning probe microscopy and a tool for nanotechnology (Review of Scientific Instruments, 2007), Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of single cells (Nature Communications, 2017)

Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using Digital Microscope to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with Digital Microscope for materials science research.

name: DMA
short description: Dynamic mechanical analysis (abbreviated DMA) is a technique used to study and characterize materials. It is most useful for studying the viscoelastic behavior of polymers. A sinusoidal stress is applied and the strain in the material is measured, allowing one to determine the complex modulus. Equipment at University in Highfield Campus (UK).
typical applications: Health Effects of Overweight and Obesity in 195 Countries over 25 Years (New England Journal of Medicine, 2017), Efficientin vitrosynthesis of biologically active RNA and RNA hybridization probes from plasmids containing a bacteriophage SP6 promoter (Nucleic Acids Research, 1984), Global, Regional, and National Cancer Incidence, Mortality, Years of Life Lost, Years Lived With Disability, and Disability, Adjusted Life, years for 32 Cancer Groups, 1990 to 2015 (JAMA Oncology, 2016), Maftools: efficient and comprehensive analysis of somatic variants in cancer (Genome Research, 2018), Sensitivity of revised diagnostic criteria for the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia (Brain, 2011)
research-oriented use: 1. Study and characterize materials using DMA in a research setting, enabling systematic data collection for chemical and molecular sciences studies. 2. Materials. It is most useful for studying the viscoelastic behavior of polymers with DMA for quantitative analysis and reproducible experimental validation.

name: DNA / Fragment Analyzer
short description: A DNA sequencer is a scientific instrument used to automate the DNA sequencing process. Given a sample of DNA, a DNA sequencer is used to determine the order of the four bases: G (guanine), C (cytosine), A (adenine) and T (thymine). This is then reported as a text string, called a read. Equipment at University of Cambridge.
typical applications: featureCounts: an efficient general purpose program for assigning sequence reads to genomic features (Bioinformatics, 2013), RSEM: accurate transcript quantification from RNA, Seq data with or without a reference genome (BMC Bioinformatics, 2011), Genome sequencing in microfabricated high, density picolitre reactors (Nature, 2005), A Robust, Simple Genotyping, by, Sequencing (GBS) Approach for High Diversity Species (PLoS ONE, 2011), voom: precision weights unlock linear model analysis tools for RNA, seq read counts (Genome biology, 2014)
research-oriented use: 1. Automate the DNA sequencing process using DNA / Fragment Analyzer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Determine the order of the four bases: G (guanine) with DNA / Fragment Analyzer for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: DNA Sequencer (NGS)
short description: DNA sequencing is the process of determining the nucleic acid sequence – the order of nucleotides in DNA. It includes any method or technology that is used to determine the order of the four bases: adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine. The advent of rapid DNA sequencing methods has greatly accelerated biological and medical research and discovery. Equipment at University in The Pirbright Institute (UK).
typical applications: Basic local alignment search tool (Journal of Molecular Biology, 1990), DNA sequencing with chain, terminating inhibitors (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 1977), Trimmomatic: a flexible trimmer for Illumina sequence data (Bioinformatics, 2014), Cutadapt removes adapter sequences from high, throughput sequencing reads (EMBnet journal, 2011), Detection of specific sequences among DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis (Journal of Molecular Biology, 1975)
research-oriented use: 1. Determine the order of the four bases: adenine using DNA Sequencer (NGS), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. The order of the four bases: adenine with DNA Sequencer (NGS) for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: DSC
short description: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) is a thermoanalytical technique in which the difference in the amount of heat required to increase the temperature of a sample and a reference is measured as a function of temperature. Both the sample and reference are maintained at nearly the same temperature throughout the experiment. Generally, the temperature program for a DSC analysis is designed such that the sample holder temperature increases linearly as a function of time. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: Preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta, analysis protocols (PRISMA, P) 2015 statement (Systematic Reviews, 2015), Accurate spin, dependent electron liquid correlation energies for local spin density calculations: a critical analysis (Canadian Journal of Physics, 1980), Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta, Analyses: The PRISMA Statement (Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 2009), Global, regional, and national incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability for 354 diseases and injuries for 195 countries and territories, 1990–2017: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2017 (The Lancet, 2018), Global, regional, and national incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability for 328 diseases and injuries for 195 countries, 1990–2016: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2016 (The Lancet, 2017)
research-oriented use: 1. * Directory of Social Change, a British charity * Down Syndrome Centre, a registered charity in Ireland * Dschang Airport (IATA code), in Cameroon *Dollar Shave Club, an American company.

name: DVS Analyzer
short description: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP, MS) is a type of mass spectrometry that uses an inductively coupled plasma to ionize the sample. It atomizes the sample and creates atomic and small polyatomic ions, which are then detected. It is known and used for its ability to detect metals and several non, metals in liquid samples at very low concentrations. Equipment at Imperial College London.
typical applications: Sorting Signals, N, Terminal Modifications and Abundance of the Chloroplast Proteome (PLoS ONE, 2008), Poly(fluorenyl aryl piperidinium) membranes and ionomers for anion exchange membrane fuel cells (Nature Communications, 2021), Artificial intelligence in recommender systems (Complex & Intelligent Systems, 2020), Finding a roadmap to achieve large neuromorphic hardware systems (Frontiers in Neuroscience, 2013), A CRISPR screen defines a signal peptide processing pathway required by flaviviruses (Nature, 2016)
research-oriented use: 1. Its ability to detect metals and several non, metals in liquid samples at very low concentrations using DVS Analyzer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Metals and several non, metals in liquid samples at very low concentrations with DVS Analyzer for reproducible analytical measurements and experimental validation.

name: E-Beam Lithography (EBL)
short description: Electron, beam lithography (often abbreviated as e, beam lithography or EBL) is the practice of scanning a focused beam of electrons to draw custom shapes on a surface covered with an electron, sensitive film called a resist (exposing). The electron beam changes the solubility of the resist, enabling selective removal of either the exposed or non, exposed regions of the resist by immersing it in a solvent (developing). The purpose, as with photolithography, is to create very small structures in the resist that can subsequently be transferred to the substrate material, often by etching. Equipment at University of Cambridge.
typical applications: Unconventional superconductivity in magic, angle graphene superlattices (Nature, 2018), WSXM: A software for scanning probe microscopy and a tool for nanotechnology (Review of Scientific Instruments, 2007), Nanoscale thermal transport (Journal of Applied Physics, 2003), Perpendicular switching of a single ferromagnetic layer induced by in, plane current injection (Nature, 2011), Single, and multi, wall carbon nanotube field, effect transistors (Applied Physics Letters, 1998)
research-oriented use: 1. Characterizing the electrochemical properties of battery electrode materials using E, Beam Lithography (EBL) for energy storage research. 2. Studying corrosion behavior and surface passivation of metal alloys with E, Beam Lithography (EBL) techniques in materials engineering.

name: EBSD Detector System
short description: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) is a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) technique used to study the crystallographic structure of materials. EBSD is carried out in a scanning electron microscope equipped with an EBSD detector comprising at least a phosphorescent screen, a compact lens and a low, light camera. In the microscope an incident beam of electrons hits a tilted sample. Equipment at University College London.
typical applications: Fundamentals and advances in magnesium alloy corrosion (Progress in Materials Science, 2017), Recent advances and applications of deep learning methods in materials science (npj Computational Materials, 2022), Grain structure control during metal 3D printing by high, intensity ultrasound (Nature Communications, 2020), The application of electron backscatter diffraction and orientation contrast imaging in the SEM to textural problems in rocks (American Mineralogist, 1999), Deviation from high, entropy configurations in the atomic distributions of a multi, principal, element alloy (Nature Communications, 2015)
research-oriented use: 1. Imaging cellular ultrastructure or tissue morphology at high resolution using EBSD Detector System to study biological processes such as cell division, protein localization, or pathogen invasion. 2. Characterizing surface topography and defect structures of nanomaterials or thin films with EBSD Detector System for materials science research.

name: EDM Machine
short description: Schiaparelli EDM (Italian: [skjapaˈrɛlli]) was a failed Entry, Descent, and Landing Demonstrator Module (EDM) of the ExoMars programme—a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Russian Space Agency Roscosmos. It was built in Italy and was intended to test technology for future soft landings on the surface of Mars. It also had a limited but focused science payload that would have measured atmospheric electricity on Mars and local meteorological conditions. Equipment at University of Strathclyde.
typical applications: Review of selective laser melting: Materials and applications (Applied Physics Reviews, 2015), Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation (SECCHI) (Space Science Reviews, 2008), State of the art electrical discharge machining (EDM) (International Journal of Machine Tools and Manufacture, 2003), Condition Monitoring of Bearing Damage in Electromechanical Drive Systems by Using Motor Current Signals of Electric Motors: A Benchmark Data Set for Data, Driven Classification (PHM Society European Conference, 2016), Reconfigurable manufacturing systems: Key to future manufacturing (Journal of Intelligent Manufacturing, 2000)

name: EDX/EDS Spectrometer
short description: Energy, dispersive X, ray spectroscopy (EDS, EDX, EDXS or XEDS), sometimes called energy dispersive X, ray analysis (EDXA or EDAX) or energy dispersive X, ray microanalysis (EDXMA), is an analytical technique used for the elemental analysis or chemical characterization of a sample. It relies on an interaction of some source of X, ray excitation and a sample. Its characterization capabilities are due in large part to the fundamental principle that each element has a unique atomic structure allowing a unique set of peaks on its electromagnetic emission spectrum (which is the main principle of spectroscopy). Equipment at University College London.
typical applications: X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopic chemical state quantification of mixed nickel metal, oxide and hydroxide systems (Surface and Interface Analysis, 2009), Polyaniline, intercalated manganese dioxide nanolayers as a high, performance cathode material for an aqueous zinc, ion battery (Nature Communications, 2018), Recommendations for reporting "black carbon" measurements (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2013), The origin of high efficiency in low, temperature solution, processable bilayer organometal halide hybrid solar cells (Energy & Environmental Science, 2013), MXene molecular sieving membranes for highly efficient gas separation (Nature Communications, 2018)
research-oriented use: 1. The elemental analysis or chemical characterization of a sample using EDX/EDS Spectrometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating EDX/EDS Spectrometer into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: EEG System
short description: EEG, fMRI (short for EEG, correlated fMRI or electroencephalography, correlated functional magnetic resonance imaging) is a multimodal neuroimaging technique whereby EEG and fMRI data are recorded synchronously for the study of electrical brain activity in correlation with haemodynamic changes in brain during the electrical activity, be it normal function or associated with disorders. Equipment at Uk + Sbrewer@Essex University (UK).
typical applications: Clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (Neurology, 1984), FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data (Computational Intelligence and Neuroscience, 2010), Fractional Brownian Motions, Fractional Noises and Applications (SIAM Review, 1968), Coherence in Spontaneous Radiation Processes (Physical Review, 1954), ILAE classification of the epilepsies: Position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology (Epilepsia, 2017)
research-oriented use: 1. Characterizing the electrochemical properties of battery electrode materials using EEG System for energy storage research. 2. Studying corrosion behavior and surface passivation of metal alloys with EEG System techniques in materials engineering.

name: Electron Beam Ion Trap (EBIT)
short description: An ion source is a device that creates atomic and molecular ions. Ion sources are used to form ions for mass spectrometers, optical emission spectrometers, particle accelerators, ion implanters and ion engines. Equipment at Queen's University Belfast.
typical applications: Quantum cryptography (Reviews of Modern Physics, 2002), Unconventional superconductivity in magic, angle graphene superlattices (Nature, 2018), Cavity optomechanics (Reviews of Modern Physics, 2014), Stochastic resonance (Reviews of Modern Physics, 1998), The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009)
research-oriented use: 1. Form ions for mass spectrometers using Electron Beam Ion Trap (EBIT), enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating Electron Beam Ion Trap (EBIT) into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Elemental Analyzer (CHN)
short description: Combustion analysis is a method used in both organic chemistry and analytical chemistry to determine the elemental composition (more precisely empirical formula) of a pure organic compound by combusting the sample under conditions where the resulting combustion products can be quantitatively analyzed. Once the number of moles of each combustion product has been determined the empirical formula or a partial empirical formula of the original compound can be calculated. Applications for combustion analysis involve only the elements of carbon (C), hydrogen (H), nitrogen (N), and sulfur (S) as combustion of materials containing them convert these elements to their oxidized form (CO2, H2O, NO or NO2, and SO2) under high temperature high oxygen conditions. Equipment at University of East Anglia.
typical applications: The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009), Electron Energy, Loss Spectroscopy in the Electron Microscope (Physics Today, 1987), Physics of thin, film ferroelectric oxides (Reviews of Modern Physics, 2005), Biodiversity on the Rocks: Macrofauna Inhabiting Authigenic Carbonate at Costa Rica Methane Seeps (PLoS ONE, 2015), Black carbon or brown carbon? The nature of light, absorbing carbonaceous aerosols (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2006)

Applying Elemental Analyzer (CHN) — combustion analysis is a method used in both organic chemistry and analytical chemistry to determine the elemental composition (more precisely empirical formula) of a pure organic compound by combusting the sample under conditions where the resulting combustion products can be quantitatively analyzed — to investigate research questions in chemical and molecular sciences. 2. Employing Elemental Analyzer (CHN) as part of an integrated analytical workflow for comparative analysis and method validation in research.

name: Environmental Chamber
short description: Instrumentation is a collective term for measuring instruments, used for indicating, measuring, and recording physical quantities. It is also a field of study about the art and science about making measurement instruments, involving the related areas of metrology, automation, and control theory. The term has its origins in the art and science of scientific instrument, making. Equipment at University of Hertfordshire.
typical applications: Occurrence of the potent mutagens 2, nitrobenzanthrone and 3, nitrobenzanthrone in fine airborne particles (Scientific Reports, 2019), Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts: a versatile cell system for transient gene expression analysis (Nature Protocols, 2007), Human mesenchymal stem cells modulate allogeneic immune cell responses (Blood, 2004), Genome sequence of the palaeopolyploid soybean (Nature, 2010), The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009)
research-oriented use: 1. Automating high, throughput compound screening using Environmental Chamber for drug discovery campaigns. 2. Deploying Environmental Chamber for reproducible sample preparation in large, scale genomics or proteomics studies.

name: EPR Spectrometer
short description: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) or electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy is a method for studying materials that have unpaired electrons. The basic concepts of EPR are analogous to those of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), but the spins excited are those of the electrons instead of the atomic nuclei. EPR spectroscopy is useful for analyzing metal ions and organic radicals (compounds with unpaired electrons). Equipment at Imperial College London.
typical applications: Stochastic resonance (Reviews of Modern Physics, 1998), A highly resolved, oxygen‐evolving photosystem II preparation from spinach thylakoid membranes (FEBS Letters, 1981), Glossary of terms used in physical organic chemistry (IUPAC Recommendations 1994) (Pure and Applied Chemistry, 1994), Hollow MnO2 as a tumor, microenvironment, responsive biodegradable nano, platform for combination therapy favoring antitumor immune responses (Nature Communications, 2017), Oxidation of tetrahydrobiopterin leads to uncoupling of endothelial cell nitric oxide synthase in hypertension (Journal of Clinical Investigation, 2003)
research-oriented use: 1. Metal ions and organic radicals (compounds with unpaired electrons) using EPR Spectrometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. Integrating EPR Spectrometer into multi, instrument measurement workflows for comprehensive sample characterization and comparative studies.

name: Fatigue Testing Machine
short description: In mechanics and physics, shock is a sudden acceleration caused, for example, by impact, drop, kick, earthquake, or explosion. Shock is a transient physical excitation. A mechanical shock typically consists of a short, duration, high, magnitude acceleration event that can cause structural deformation or failure in components. Equipment at University College London.
typical applications: WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis (BMC Bioinformatics, 2008), Development and Distortion of Malaysian Public, Private Partnerships: Patronage, Privatised Profits and Pitfalls DOI: 10.1111/j.1467, 8500.2009.00655.x (Intellectum (Universidad de La Sabana), 2010), VI. The phenomena of rupture and flow in solids (Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London Series A Containing Papers of a Mathematical or Physical Character, 1921), A survey of transfer learning (Journal Of Big Data, 2016), Efficacy and Safety of Nintedanib in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (New England Journal of Medicine, 2014)

Applying Fatigue Testing Machine — in mechanics and physics, shock is a sudden acceleration caused, for example, by impact, drop, kick, earthquake, or explosion — to investigate research questions in physics and photonics. 2. Employing Fatigue Testing Machine as part of an integrated analytical workflow for comparative analysis and method validation in research.

name: Flow Cytometer
short description: Flow cytometry (FC) is a technique used to detect and measure the physical and chemical characteristics of a population of cells or particles. In this process, a sample containing cells or particles is suspended in a fluid and injected into the flow cytometer instrument. The sample is focused to ideally flow one cell at a time through a laser beam, where the light scattered is characteristic to the cells and their components. Equipment at University in Southampton General Hospital (UK).
typical applications: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles 2018 (MISEV2018): a position statement of the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles and update of the MISEV2014 guidelines (Journal of Extracellular Vesicles, 2018), Neutrophil emigration in the skin, lungs, and peritoneum: different requirements for CD11/CD18 revealed by CD18, deficient mice. (PubMed, 1997), CellProfiler: image analysis software for identifying and quantifying cell phenotypes (Genome biology, 2006), Dysregulation of Immune Response in Patients With Coronavirus 2019 (COVID, 19) in Wuhan, China (Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2020), Estimating the population abundance of tissue, infiltrating immune and stromal cell populations using gene expression (Genome biology, 2016)
research-oriented use: 1. Detect and measure the physical and chemical characteristics of a population of cells or particles using Flow Cytometer, enabling systematic investigation and quantitative data collection in research studies. 2. It is a form of electron spectroscopy that relies on the Auger effect, based on the analysis of energetic electrons emitted from an excited atom after a series of internal relaxation events. The Auger effect was discovered independently by both Lise Meitner and Pierre Auger in the 1920s.

name: Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Spectrometer
short description: Coherent anti, Stokes Raman spectroscopy, also called Coherent anti, Stokes Raman scattering spectroscopy (CARS), is a form of spectroscopy used primarily in chemistry, physics and related fields. name: Cathodoluminescence
short description: Cathodoluminescence is an optical and electromagnetic phenomenon in which electrons impacting on a luminescent material such as a phosphor, cause the emission of photons which may have wavelengths in the visible spectrum. Cathodoluminescence is the inverse of the photoelectric effect, in which electron emission is induced by irradiation with photons.

name: Cyclic Voltammetry
short description: In electrochemistry, cyclic voltammetry (CV) is a type of voltammetric measurement where the potential of the working electrode is ramped linearly versus time. Unlike in linear sweep voltammetry, after the set potential is reached in a CV experiment, the working electrode's potential is ramped in the opposite direction to return to the initial potential. These cycles in potential are repeated until the voltammetric trace reaches a cyclic steady state.

short description: Dynamic light scattering (DLS) is a technique in physics that can be used to determine the size distribution profile of small particles in suspension or polymers in solution. In the scope of DLS, temporal fluctuations are usually analyzed using the intensity or photon autocorrelation function (also known as photon correlation spectroscopy – PCS or quasi, elastic light scattering – QELS). name: Electron Energy Loss Spectrometer
short description: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) is a form of electron microscopy in which a material is exposed to a beam of electrons with a known, narrow range of kinetic energies. name: Resonance Raman Spectrometer
short description: Resonance Raman spectroscopy (RR spectroscopy or RRS) is a variant of Raman spectroscopy in which the incident photon energy is close in energy to an electronic transition of a compound or material under examination. This similarity in energy (resonance) leads to greatly increased intensity of the Raman scattering of certain vibrational modes, compared to ordinary Raman spectroscopy. name: X-ray Fluorescence
short description: X, ray fluorescence (XRF) is the emission of characteristic "secondary" (or fluorescent) X, rays from a material that has been excited by being bombarded with high, energy X, rays or gamma rays. name: Neutron Activation
short description: Neutron activation is the process in which neutron radiation induces radioactivity in materials, and occurs when atomic nuclei capture free neutrons, becoming heavier and entering excited states. The excited nucleus decays immediately by emitting gamma rays, or particles such as beta particles, alpha particles, fission products, and neutrons (in nuclear fission). Thus, the process of neutron capture, even after any intermediate decay, often results in the formation of an unstable activation product.

name: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR)
short description: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a physical phenomenon in which nuclei in a strong constant magnetic field are disturbed by a weak oscillating magnetic field (in the near field) and respond by producing an electromagnetic signal with a frequency characteristic of the magnetic field at the nucleus. This process occurs near resonance, when the oscillation frequency matches the intrinsic frequency of the nuclei, which depends on the strength of the static magnetic field, the chemical environment, and the magnetic properties of the isotope involved; in practical applications with static magnetic fields up to ca. 20 tesla, the frequency is similar to VHF and UHF television broadcasts (60–1000 MHz).

name: Refractive Index
short description: In optics, the refractive index (also called refraction index or index of refraction), often denoted n, is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum (c) to the speed of light in a given optical medium (v), n=c/v. The refractive index determines how much the path of light is bent, or refracted, when entering a material, as described by Snell's law of refraction, n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2, where θ1 and θ2 are the angle of incidence and angle of refraction, respectively, of a ray crossing the interface between two media with refractive indices n1 and n2. The refractive indices also determine the amount of light that is reflected when reaching the interface, as well as the critical angle for total internal reflection, their intensity (Fresnel equations) and Brewster's angle.

name: 10–20 system (EEG)
short description: The 10–20 system or International 10–20 system is an internationally recognized method to describe and apply the location of scalp electrodes in the context of an EEG exam, polysomnograph sleep study, or voluntary lab research. This method was developed to maintain standardized testing methods ensuring that a subject's study outcomes (clinical or research) could be compiled, reproduced, and effectively analyzed and compared using the scientific method. It also ensures consistency in EEG measurements despite the variety of head shapes and sizes.

Non, labeled EF5 has been extensively used in immunohistochemical studies for several years and its hypoxia specificity has been comprehensively evaluated The 18F, radiolabeled derivative of EF5 is being studied for its possibility to be used in positron emission tomography (PET) to detect low levels of oxygen in brain tumors and several other malignant tumors.

short description: The 2m Bubble Chamber was a device used in conjunction with CERN's 25 GeV Proton Synchrotron (PS) machine to study high, energy physics. It was decided to build this chamber in 1958 with a large team of physicists, engineers, technicians and designers led by Charles Peyrou. short description: In semiconductor manufacturing, the 2 nm process is the MOSFET (metal–oxide–semiconductor field, effect transistor) die shrink after the 3 nm process node. The term "2 nanometer", or alternatively "20 angstrom" (a term used by Intel), has no relation to any actual physical feature (such as gate length, metal pitch or gate pitch) of the transistors. According to the projections contained in the 2021 update of the International Roadmap for Devices and Systems published by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), a "2.1 nm node range label" is expected to have a contacted gate pitch of 45 nanometers and a tightest metal pitch of 20 nanometers.

It had been controlled by Yasuo Yamamoto, an anti, nuclear protester from Fukui Prefecture. Yamamoto flew the drone there carrying sand containing caesium from Fukushima prefecture on April 9, but the drone was not discovered until April 22.

name: 3D Content Retrieval
short description: A 3D Content Retrieval system is a computer system for browsing, searching and retrieving three dimensional digital contents (e.g.: Computer, aided design, molecular biology models, and cultural heritage 3D scenes,  etc.) from a large database of digital images. The most original way of doing 3D content retrieval uses methods to add description text to 3D content files such as the content file name, link text, and the web page title so that related 3D content can be found through text retrieval. Because of the inefficiency of manually annotating 3D files, researchers have investigated ways to automate the annotation process and provide a unified standard to create text descriptions for 3D contents.

name: 3D Morphable Model
short description: In computer vision and computer graphics, the 3D Morphable Model (3DMM) is a generative technique that uses methods of statistical shape analysis to model 3D objects. The model follows an analysis, by, synthesis approach over a dataset of 3D example shapes of a single class of objects (e.g., face, hand). The main prerequisite is that all the 3D shapes are in a dense point, to, point correspondence, namely each point has the same semantical meaning over all the shapes.

Generally, 3D bioprinting uses a layer, by, layer method to deposit materials known as bio, inks to create tissue, like structures that are later used in various medical and tissue engineering fields. 3D bioprinting covers a broad range of bioprinting techniques and biomaterials.
